biography: Dimitri Collin's journey began not on asphalt, but on the muddy, unpredictable tracks of Belgian kart cross. Born in a small village outside of Liège, Dimitri spent his youth tinkering with engines alongside his father, a local mechanic. His first taste of competition came at 16, entering local kart cross events with a machine cobbled together from spare parts. While raw speed wasn't always his forte, his uncanny ability to nurse a vehicle through the roughest terrain quickly earned him respect. He rose through the ranks, securing several regional championships. However, Dimitri never quite made the jump to higher-profile motorsport series. Sponsorships proved elusive, and a growing family demanded stability. Now in his mid-thirties, he still competes in Kart Cross, a familiar face, respected for his experience, even if his best days are behind him. While the dream of international fame has faded, the passion for the sport remains, a testament to his enduring love for racing.
drivingStyle: Dimitri's driving style is best described as pragmatic and consistent. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or daring late-braking maneuvers. Instead, he focuses on maintaining a smooth, predictable line, minimizing wear and tear on his vehicle. He excels at tire management, often coaxing a few extra laps out of a set when others are struggling. Under pressure, Dimitri tends to tighten up, becoming even more conservative, sometimes to his detriment. He prioritizes finishing the race and accruing points over taking risks for a potential win.

rivalries.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
rivalries.reason: A longstanding rivalry stemming from a controversial collision in the 2015 Belgian Kart Cross Championship finale, costing Dimitri the title.

rivalries.name: Annelies Van den Broeck
rivalries.reason: A fierce competitor known for her aggressive driving, Annelies often clashes with Dimitri's more cautious approach, leading to frequent on-track battles.

rivalries.name: Thierry Lecomte
rivalries.reason: A young up-and-comer whose raw speed and disregard for equipment often puts him at odds with Dimitri's more calculated approach to racing.

quirks: Always wears the same faded blue racing gloves, claiming they bring him luck.
Refuses to start a race without meticulously cleaning his visor with a specific brand of Belgian beer.
Has a habit of talking to his kart before each race, offering words of encouragement and promises of careful driving.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about going the fastest, it's about lasting the longest."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2012 Wallonian Kart Cross Championship after a season-long battle with Jean-Pierre Dubois. He secured the victory with a perfectly executed final lap maneuver, showcasing his tactical prowess.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2018 Belgian Kart Cross Championship while leading the final race, due to a mechanical failure. The incident effectively ended his hopes of securing another major title.
